sanskrit: mahat tad ulbaṁ sthaviram tad āsīd yenāviṣṭitaḥ praviveśithāpaḥ | viśvā apaśyad bahudhā te agne jātavedas tanvo deva ekaḥ ||
english: Great and thick was that membrane — great it was — wrapped in which you entered the waters. One god alone, O Agni Jātavedas, saw all your bodies manifested in many forms.

sanskrit: ko mā dadarśa katamaḥ sa devo yo me tanvo bahudhā paryapaśyat | kvāha mitrāvaruṇā kṣiyanty agner viśvāḥ samidho devayānīḥ ||
english: Who saw me? Which was that god who beheld my bodies manifested in many forms? Where dwell, O Mitra and Varuṇa, all the divine fuel-faggots of Agni that lead to the gods?

sanskrit: aicchāma tvā bahudhā jātavedaḥ praviṣṭam agne apsv oṣadhīṣu | taṁ tvā yamo acikec citrabhāno daśāntaruṣyād atiroсamānam ||
english: We sought you, O Jātavedas, hidden in many forms, entered, O Agni, into the waters, into the plants. Yama revealed you, O Citrabhānu, as you shone forth glowing from the ten kindling-woods.

sanskrit: hotrād ahaṁ varuṇa bibhyad āyam ned eva mā yunajann atra devāḥ | tasya me tanvo bahudhā niviṣṭā etam artham na ciketāham agniḥ ||
english: I came here, O Varuṇa, fleeing from the office of Hotṛ, lest the gods should harness me to that task. My bodies entered in many places — of that matter I, Agni, was unaware.

sanskrit: ehi manur devayur yajñakāmo araṁkṛtyā tamasi kṣeṣy agne | sugān pathaḥ kṛṇuhi devayānān vaha havyāni sumanasyamānaḥ ||
english: Come! Manu, pious and desirous of sacrifice, is ready; thou dwellest in the darkness, O Agni. Make the paths easy that lead to the gods; willingly convey the oblations.

sanskrit: agneḥ pūrve bhrātaro artham etam rathīvādhvānam anv āvarīvuḥ | tasmād bhiyā varuṇa dūram āyam gauro na kṣepnor avije jyāyāḥ ||
english: The earlier brothers of Agni perished following this same course like a charioteer on the road. Therefore, O Varuṇa, I came far away in fear, trembling like a gayal from the bowstring of the archer.

sanskrit: kurmas ta āyur ajaram yad agne yathā yukto jātavedo na riṣyāḥ | athā vahāsi sumanasyamāno bhāgam devebhyo haviṣaḥ sujāta ||
english: We shall grant you ageless life, O Agni, so that, O Jātavedas, harnessed, you shall not be harmed. Then joyfully you shall carry the share of the oblation to the gods, O noble-born.

sanskrit: prayājān me anuyājāmś ca kevalān ūrjasvantam haviṣo datta bhāgam | ghṛtam cāpām puruṣam cauṣadhīnām agneś ca dīrgham āyur astu devāḥ ||
english: Give me the prayājas and the anuyājas alone as my exclusive, vigorous share of the oblation — ghee, and the essence of waters and plants. And may Agni's life be long, O gods.

sanskrit: tava prayājā anuyājāś ca kevala ūrjasvanto haviṣaḥ santu bhāgāḥ | tavāgne yajño 'yam astu sarvas tubhyam namantām pradiśaś catasraḥ ||
english: Yours alone shall be the prayājas and the anuyājas as vigorous shares of the oblation. Let this entire sacrifice be yours, O Agni; let the four quarters bow down to you.

sanskrit: viśve devāḥ śāstana mā yatheha hotā vṛto manavai yan niṣadya | pra me brūta bhāgadheyam yathā vo yena pathā havyam ā vo vahāni ||
english: All you gods, instruct me how I, chosen as Hotṛ by Manu, shall sit and perform the rite. Tell me what the share-apportionment is to you, by what path I may bring the oblations to you.

sanskrit: aham hotā ny asīdam yajīyān viśve devā maruto mā junanti | ahar-ahar aśvinādhvaryavam vām brahmā samid bhavati sāhutir vām ||
english: I, the mightier Hotṛ, took my seat; all the gods and Maruts urge me on. Day after day the Adhvaryu rite is yours, O Aśvins; the Brahman becomes the kindling-wood and the offering is yours.

sanskrit: ayam yo hotā kir u sa yamasya kam apy ūhe yat samañjanti devāḥ | ahar-ahar jāyate māsi-māsy athā devā dadhire havyavāham ||
english: This one who is the Hotṛ — who then is he of Yama? Whom do they adorn when the gods anoint? Day after day, month after month he is born anew — the gods have appointed him carrier of oblations.

sanskrit: māṁ devā dadhire havyavāham apamlukta bahu kṛcchrā carantam | agnir vidvān yajñam naḥ kalpayāti pañcayāmaṁ trivṛtam saptatatantum ||
english: Me the gods appointed carrier of oblations, though long hidden, wandering through many difficulties. Agni, knowing all, shall order our sacrifice — of five courses, threefold, and sevenfold in thread.

sanskrit: ā vo yakṣy amṛtatvam suvīram yathā vo devā varivah karāṇi | ā bāhvor vajram indrasya dheyām athemā viśvāḥ pṛtanā jayāti ||
english: I shall worship immortality and heroic strength for you so that I may make wide space for you, O gods. I shall place Indra's thunderbolt in his arms; then shall he conquer all these hosts.

sanskrit: trīṇi śatā trī sahasrāṇy agnim triṁśac ca devā nava cāsaparyan | aukṣan ghṛtair astṛṇan barhir asmā ād id dhotāram ny asādayanta ||
english: Three hundreds and three thousands — thirty and nine gods together — attended to Agni; they sprinkled him with ghee, spread the sacred grass for him, and then installed him as Hotṛ.

sanskrit: yam aicchāma manasā so 'yam āgād yajñasya vidvān paruṣaś cikitvān | sa no yakṣad devatātā yajīyān ni hi ṣatsad antaraḥ pūrvo asmat ||
english: He whom we sought in our mind has come — knowing the sacrifice, wise, the many-jointed, the discerning. He, mightier in worship, shall sacrifice for us at the divine assembly; let him take his seat as our closest, foremost.

sanskrit: arādhi hotā niṣadā yajīyān abhi prayāṁsi sudhitāni hi khyat | yajāmahai yajñiyān hanta devām̐ īḻāmahā īḍyām̐ ājyena ||
english: The Hotṛ has taken his seat, the worthier one; he beholds the well-set offerings. Come! let us worship the gods worthy of worship; let us praise with ghee those who merit praise.

sanskrit: sādhvīm akar devavītim no adya yajñasya jihvām avidāma guhyām | sa āyur āgāt surabhir vasāno bhadrām akar devahūtim no adya ||
english: He made our divine communion excellent today; we have found the hidden tongue of the sacrifice. He has come bearing life, clad in fragrance; he made our invocation of the gods auspicious today.

sanskrit: tad adya vācaḥ prathamam masīya yenāsurām̐ abhi devā asāma | ūrjāda uta yajñiyāsaḥ pañca janā mama hotram juṣadhvam ||
english: Let me today utter first that speech by which the gods overpowered the Asuras. O eaters of vigour, and you who are worthy of sacrifice — ye five peoples, delight in my Hotṛ-call.

sanskrit: pañca janā mama hotram juṣantām gojātā uta ye yajñiyāsaḥ | pṛthivī naḥ pārthivāt pātv aṁhaso 'ntarikṣam divyāt pātv asmān ||
english: Let the five peoples delight in my Hotṛ-call — those born of cattle and those worthy of sacrifice. May the Earth protect us from earthly distress; may the Atmosphere protect us from what comes from heaven.

sanskrit: tantum tanvan rajaso bhānum anv ihi jyotiṣmataḥ patho rakṣa dhiyā kṛtān | anulbaṇam vayata joguvām apo manur bhava janayā daivyam janam ||
english: Spinning the thread, follow the gleam of the sky's expanse; protect the luminous paths made by the mind. Weave, without breaks, the waters that have been sung; be Manu, beget the divine people.

sanskrit: akṣānaho nahyatanota somyā iṣkṛṇudhvam raśanā ota piṁśata | aṣṭāvandhuram vahatābhito ratham yena devāso anayann abhi priyam ||
english: Tie the axle-pins and fasten them, O ye who have soma; trim the reins and adorn them. Drive from both sides the eight-yoked chariot whereby the gods drove toward the beloved.

sanskrit: aśmanvatī rīyate sam rabhadhvam ut tiṣṭhata pra taratā sakhāyaḥ | atrā jahāma ye asann aśevāḥ śivān vayam ut taremābhi vājān ||
english: The stony river flows — grasp one another, rise up, cross over, O friends! Here let us leave behind those who were unfit; we shall cross over toward the blessings, toward the prizes.

sanskrit: tvaṣṭā māyā ved apasām apastamo bibhrat pātrā devapānāni śaṁtamā | śiśīte nūnam paraśum svāyasam yena vṛścād etaśo brahmaṇas patiḥ ||
english: Tvaṣṭṛ knows the wisdom — the most artful of craftsmen — bearing the vessels, most comforting, fit for the gods to drink from. He now sharpens the iron axe with which the Etaśa-horse, Lord of Prayer, shall cut.

sanskrit: sato nūnam kavayaḥ sam śiśīta vāśībhir yābhir amṛtāya takṣatha | vidvāṁsaḥ padā guhyāni kartana yena devāso amṛtatvam ānaśuḥ ||
english: Now, O sages who are being perfected, sharpen yourselves with the chisels with which you work for immortality. Knowing, cut out the hidden tracks by which the gods attained immortality.

sanskrit: garbhe yoṣām adadhur vatsam āsany apīcyena manasota jihvayā | sa viśvāhā sumanā yogyā abhi siṣāsanir vanate kāra ij jitim ||
english: They placed in the womb of the woman the calf, hidden with secret mind and tongue. He who is well-disposed, ever seeking union, reaches victory — the worshipper wins it alone.

sanskrit: tām su te kīrtim maghavan mahitvā yat tvā bhīte rodasī ahvayetām | prāvo devām̐ ātiro dāsam ojaḥ prajāyai tvasyai yad aśikṣa indra ||
english: Well do we proclaim that glory of yours, O Maghavan, in your greatness — when both the frightened worlds called upon you. You protected the gods, overpowered the Dāsa with your force; for that offspring you trained, O Indra.

sanskrit: yad acaras tanvā vāvṛdhāno balānīndra prabruvāṇo janeṣu | māyet sā te yāni yuddhāny āhur nādya śatrum nanu purā vivitse ||
english: When you went about growing in your own body, declaring your powers, O Indra, among the peoples — may it not be that the battles they speak of come to nothing; you have not yet ceased to know the enemy.

sanskrit: ka u nu te mahimanaḥ samasyāsmat pūrva ṛṣayo 'ntam āpuḥ | yan mātaram ca pitaram ca sākam ajanayathās tanvaḥ svāyāḥ ||
english: Who of the earlier sages before us ever reached the full measure of your greatness — you who together generated both your mother and your father from your own body?

sanskrit: catvāri te asuryāṇi nāmādābhyāni mahiṣasya santi | tvam aṅga tāni viśvāni vitsel yebhiḥ karmāṇi maghavañ cakartha ||
english: Your four mighty names, belonging to the bull, are inviolable. Only you, O Maghavan, know them all, those names by which you performed your deeds.

sanskrit: tvaṁ viśvā dadhiṣe kevalāni yāny āvir yā ca guhā vasūni | kāmam in me maghavan mā vi tārīs tvam ājñātā tvam indrāsi dātā ||
english: You alone hold all the riches — those that are manifest and those that are hidden. Do not, O Maghavan, disappoint my desire; you, Indra, are the knower and you are the giver.

sanskrit: yo adadhāj jyotiṣi jyotir antar yo asṛjan madhunā sam madhūni | adha priyam śūṣam indrāya manma brahmaharṣṭo bṛhadu kthād avāci ||
english: He who placed light within light, who mingled sweetnesses with sweetness — to that dear Indra this praise, this mighty utterance, was spoken from the brahman-made high hymn.

sanskrit: dūre tan nāma guhyam parācair yat tvā bhīte ahvayetām vayodhai | ud astabhnāḥ pṛthivīm dyām abhīke bhrātuḥ putrān maghavan titviṣāṇaḥ ||
english: Far away is that hidden name, in remote regions — the name by which both the frightened ones, growing old, called upon you. You propped up both earth and sky together, O Maghavan, blazing with power, protecting your brother's sons.

sanskrit: mahat tan nāma guhyam puruspṛg yena bhūtam janayo yena bhavyam | pratnam jātam jyotir yad asya priyam priyāḥ sam aviśanta pañca ||
english: Great is that hidden name, widely touching all, by which what was and what shall be comes to be. The ancient, born light that is dear to him — the dear five entered into union.

sanskrit: ā rodasī apṛṇād ota madhyam pañca devām̐ ṛtuśaḥ sapta-sapta | catutriṁśatā purudhā vi caṣṭe sarūpeṇa jyotiṣā vivratena ||
english: He filled both the worlds and the middle space; the five gods he filled seasonally, seven by seven. With thirty-four he views them in manifold forms, by a light of uniform appearance and varied ordinance.

sanskrit: yad uṣa auchaḥ prathamā vibhānām ajanayo yena puṣṭasya puṣṭam | yat te jāmitvam avaram parasyā mahan mahaty asuratvaṁ ekam ||
english: When you, Dawn, first shone forth among the radiant ones, you generated nourishment from nourishment. What is the lesser kinship, what the higher? Great, for the great one, is that single Asura-power.

sanskrit: vidhuṁ dadrāṇam samane bahūnām yuvānam santam palito jagāra | devasya paśya kāvyam mahitvādyā mamāra sa hyaḥ sam āna ||
english: The wandering moon, sleeping at the assembly of many, though young, was devoured by the grey one. Behold the divine mystery in its greatness — he who died today was alive yesterday.

sanskrit: śākmanā śāko aruṇaḥ suparṇa ā yo mahaḥ śūraḥ sanād anīḷaḥ ||  yac ciketa satyam it tan na mogham vasu spārham uta jeto uta dātā ||
english: By his own might, the reddish fair-winged hero, great, brave, forever unassailable — whatever he perceives, that truly is not fruitless; he is winner and giver of desirable wealth.

sanskrit: aibhir dade vṛṣṇyā pauṁsyāni yebhir aukṣad vṛtrahatyāya vajrī | ye karmaṇaḥ kriyamāṇasya mahnā ṛtakarmam udajāyanta devāḥ ||
english: With these he received his bull-powers and manly vigour, wherewith the Vajra-bearer anointed himself for the slaying of Vṛtra. Those gods who were born through the greatness of deeds being performed — they performed their acts according to Ṛta.

sanskrit: yujā karmāṇi janayan viśvaujā aśastihā viśvamanās turāṣāṭ ||  pītvī somasya diva ā vṛdhānaḥ śūro nir yudhādhamad dasyūn ||
english: Generating deeds in union, all-powerful, slayer of the wicked, all-minded, overpowering the strong — having drunk the Soma, growing great from the sky, the hero drove out the Dasyus from battle.

sanskrit: idam ta ekam para ū ta ekam tṛtīyena jyotiṣā sam viśasva | samveśane tanvaś cārur edhi priyo devānām parame janitre ||
english: This one is yours, and yet another is beyond — enter union with the third light. At the gathering-in be lovely in body; be dear to the gods in the highest birthplace.

sanskrit: tanūṣ ṭe vājin tanvam nayantī vāmam asmabhyam dhātu śarma tubhyam | ahṛto maho dharaṇāya devān divīva jyotiḥ svam ā mimīyāḥ ||
english: She who leads your body, O Vājin, may she grant us beauty, shelter to you. Untroubled, for upholding the great gods, measure out your own light as in the sky.

sanskrit: vājy asi vājinena suveniḥ suvitaḥ stomam suvito divam gāḥ | suvito dharma prathamānu satyā suvito devān suvito 'nu patma ||
english: You are the swift horse, fleet by means of the fleet; well-sped, you delight in the hymn of praise; well-sped, you go to heaven. Well-sped, follow the primeval truths of dharma; well-sped among the gods, well-sped along the path.

sanskrit: mahimna eṣām pitaraś caneśire devā deveṣv adadhur api kratum | sam avavyacur uta yāny atviṣur aiṣām tanūṣu ni viviśuḥ punaḥ ||
english: Not even the Fathers could control the greatness of these; the gods placed their will in the gods. What they covered and what they set ablaze entered back again into their bodies.

sanskrit: sahobhir viśvam pari cakramū rajaḥ pūrvā dhāmāny amitā mimānāḥ | tanūṣu viśvā bhuvanā ni yemire prāsārayanta purudha prajā anu ||
english: With their powers they circled all the expanse of the sky, measuring the primeval, immeasurable stations. They held all the worlds within their bodies; they stretched them out manifoldly among the offspring.

sanskrit: dvidhā sūnavo asuram svarvid am āsthāpayanta tṛtīyena karmaṇā | svām prajām pitaraḥ pitrya saha āvareṣv adadhus tantum ātatam ||
english: The sons established the Asura, the finder of heaven, in two ways by the third deed. The Fathers, together with the fathers' world, stretched the thread of their own offspring through the lower ones.

sanskrit: nāvā na kṣodaḥ pradiśaḥ pṛthivyāḥ svastibhir ati durgāṇi viśvā | svām prajām bṛhadukto mahitvāvareṣv adadhād ā pareṣu ||
english: As a ship crosses the flood, the quarters of the earth — by blessings may we pass beyond all difficulties. The one of great praise, through his greatness, established his offspring in the lower and even in the higher regions.

sanskrit: mā pra gāma patho vayam mā yajñād indra sominaḥ | māntaḥ sthur no arātayaḥ ||
english: May we not stray from the path, may we not stray from the sacrifice, O Indra, we who have pressed the Soma. May the ill-wishers not stand among us.

sanskrit: yo yajñasya prasādhanas tantur deveṣv ātat aḥ | tam āhutam naśīmahi ||
english: That thread which perfects the sacrifice, stretched out among the gods — may we attain it, duly offered.

sanskrit: mano nv ā huvāmahe nārāśaṁsena somena | pitṝṇām ca manmabhiḥ ||
english: Now we call upon the mind — with the Nārāśaṁsa-Soma, and with the praises of the Pitṛs.

sanskrit: ā ta etu manaḥ punaḥ kratve dakṣāya jīvase | jyok ca sūryam dṛśe ||
english: May your mind return again — for will, for discernment, for living, and long to behold the Sun.

sanskrit: punar naḥ pitaro mano dadātu daivyo janaḥ | jīvam vrātam sacemahi ||
english: May the Fathers restore our mind; may the divine company give it back. May we be joined with the living host.

sanskrit: vayam soma vrate tava manas tanūṣu bibhrataḥ | prajāvantaḥ sacemahi ||
english: We, O Soma, in your covenant, bearing the mind in our bodies — may we, endowed with offspring, be joined together.

sanskrit: yat te yamam vaivastvatam mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to Yama Vaivasvata — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te divam yat pṛthivīm mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the sky, to the earth — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te bhūmim caturbhṛṣṭim mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the four-cornered earth — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te catasraḥ pradiśo mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the four quarters — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te samudram arṇavam mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the ocean, the flood — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te marīcīḥ pravato mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the bright rays, to the heights — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te apo yad oṣadhīr mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the waters, to the plants — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te sūryam yad uṣasam mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the Sun, to the Dawn — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te parvatān bṛhato mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the great mountains — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te viśvam idam jagat mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to this entire universe — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te parāḥ parāvato mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to the farthest of the far regions — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: yat te bhūtam ca bhavyam ca mano jagāma dūrakam | tat ta ā vartayāmasīha kṣayāya jīvase ||
english: That mind of yours which has gone far away to what has been and what shall be — that we bring back to you here, for dwelling, for living.

sanskrit: pra tāry āyuḥ prataram navīyaḥ sthātāreva kratumatā rathasya | adha cyavāna ut tavīty artham parātaram su nirṛtir jihītām ||
english: Lengthen out your life further, newer and newer — like a good charioteer with an able-willed chariot. Then, O Cyavāna, rise up to your great purpose; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.

sanskrit: sāman nu rāye nidhi man nv annam karāmahe su purudha śravāṁsi | tā no viśvāni jaritā mamattu parātaram su nirṛtir jihītām ||
english: With a hymn we shall win wealth, a treasure of food; we shall win splendid fame in many ways. May all these things rejoice our singer; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.

sanskrit: abhī ṣv aryaḥ pauṁsyair bhavema dyaur na bhūmim girayo nājrān | tā no viśvāni jaritā ciketa parātaram su nirṛtir jihītām ||
english: May we become the chief with manly powers — as the sky does not injure the earth, nor the mountains the plains. May our singer know all these things for us; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.

sanskrit: mo ṣu ṇaḥ soma mṛtyave parā dāḥ paśyema nu sūryam uccara ntam | dyubhir hito jarimā sū no astu parātaram su nirṛtir jihītām ||
english: O Soma, do not hand us over to death; may we still see the sun rising. May old age appointed by the gods be friendly to us; let Nirṛti depart still farther away.

sanskrit: asunīte mano asmāsu dhāraya jīvātave su pra tirā na āyuḥ | rārandhi naḥ sūryasya samdṛśi ghṛtena tvam tanvam vardhayasva ||
english: O Asunīti, hold the mind within us; for living, extend our life well. Grant us the sight of the sun; with ghee do you strengthen your body.

sanskrit: asunīte punar asmāsu cakṣuḥ punaḥ prāṇam iha no dhehi bhogam | jyok paśyema sūryam uccara ntam anumate mṛḷayā naḥ svasti ||
english: O Asunīti, give back sight to us; give back breath, give enjoyment here to us. May we long see the sun rising; O Anumatī, be gracious to us, bring us well-being.

sanskrit: punar no asum pṛthivī dadātu punar dyaur devī punar antarikṣam | punar naḥ somas tanvam dadātu punaḥ pūṣā pathyām yā svastiḥ ||
english: May the Earth give back our life-breath; may the divine Sky give it back; may the Atmosphere give it back. May Soma give our body back; may Pūṣan give back the well-being that is on the path.

sanskrit: śam rodasī subandhave yahvī ṛtasya mātarā | bharatām apa yad rapo dyauḥ pṛthivi kṣamā rapo mo ṣu te kiṁ canāmamat ||
english: Blessed be both worlds for the good-kinsman — the two young mothers of Ṛta. Let them carry off whatever disease there is; O Sky, O Earth, carry off the disease; may nothing whatsoever afflict you.

sanskrit: ava dvake ava trikā divaś caranti bheṣajā | kṣamā cariṣṇv ekakam bharatām apa yad rapo dyauḥ pṛthivi kṣamā rapo mo ṣu te kiṁ canāmamat ||
english: In pairs and in triplets the healing remedies move down from heaven; some roam the earth one by one. Let them carry off whatever disease there is; O Sky, O Earth, carry off the disease; may nothing whatsoever afflict you.

sanskrit: sam indreraya gām anaḍvāham ya āvahad uśīnarāṇyā anaḥ | bharatām apa yad rapo dyauḥ pṛthivi kṣamā rapo mo ṣu te kiṁ canāmamat ||
english: O Indra, set in motion the ox who drew the cart for the queen of the Uśīnaras. Let them carry off whatever disease there is; O Sky, O Earth, carry off the disease; may nothing whatsoever afflict you.

sanskrit: ā janam tveṣasaṁdṛśam māhīnānām upastutam | aganma bibhrato namaḥ ||
english: We have approached the man of dazzling appearance, praised among the Māhīnas — bearing reverence, we have come.

sanskrit: asamātim nitośanam tveṣam niyayinam ratham | bhajerathasya satpatim ||
english: Incomparable, piercing, fierce, the chariot that follows the course — may we share in the true lord of the chariot.

sanskrit: yo janān mahiṣām̐ ivātitasthau pavīravān | utāpavīravān yudhā ||
english: He who stood over men like a buffalo, furnished with a sharp-pointed weapon — and also one with a blunted weapon in battle.

sanskrit: yasye kṣvākur upa vrate revān marāyy edhate | divīva pañca kṛṣṭayaḥ ||
english: He in whose covenant Ikṣvāku, rich in wealth, prospers and thrives — like the five peoples in the sky.

sanskrit: indra kṣatrāsamātiṣu rathaproṣṭheṣu dhāraya | divīva sūryam dṛśe ||
english: O Indra, sustain Kṣatrāsamāti in his chariots, foremost among the foremost — to be seen like the sun in the sky.

sanskrit: agastayasya nadbhyaḥ saptī yunakṣi rohitā | paṇīn ny akramīr abhi viśvān rājann arādhasa saḥ ||
english: You yoke the two red horses from the clan of Agastya. O King, you have overcome all the Paṇis who gave no gifts.

sanskrit: ayam mātāyam pitāyam jīvātur āgamat | idam tava prasarpaṇam subandhav ehi nir ihi ||
english: Here is your mother, here is your father, here the living one has come. Here is your restoration, O Subandhu — come out, come forth.

sanskrit: yathā yugam varatrayā nahyanti dharaṇāya kam | evā dādhāra te mano jīvātave na mṛtyave 'tho ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: As they bind a yoke with a threefold tie for its support — so has he held your mind fast, for living and not for dying, and for unbroken wholeness.

sanskrit: yatheyam pṛthivī mahī dādhāremān vanaspatīn | evā dādhāra te mano jīvātave na mṛtyave 'tho ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: As this great Earth holds these forest trees in place — so has he held your mind fast, for living and not for dying, and for unbroken wholeness.

sanskrit: yamād aham vaivastvatāt subandhor mana ābharam | jīvātave na mṛtyave 'tho ariṣṭatātaye ||
english: From Yama Vaivasvata I have brought back the mind of Subandhu — for living and not for dying, and for unbroken wholeness.

sanskrit: nyag vāto 'va vāti nyak tapati sūryaḥ | nīcīnam aghnyā duhe nyag bhavatu te rapaḥ ||
english: Downward the wind blows, downward the sun burns; downward the cow gives her milk — may your disease go downward.

sanskrit: ayam me hasto bhagavān ayam me bhagavattaraḥ | ayam me viśvabheṣajo 'yam śivābhimarśanaḥ ||
english: This hand of mine is full of fortune; this hand is even more fortunate. This hand contains all medicines; this hand is the gentle healing touch.
